name: a bent rusty metal sheet, broken concrete lumps, glass shards and a torn cable lying on an oil-stained patch of earth
label: wasteland_ruins/rubble-c

surfaces.part: debris clusters (rusty sheet, concrete lumps, glass, cable) at upper right, right middle and lower left

answer.evidence: The main body is a full-width 64x48 mottled earth and rubble ground texture with the same opaque width on every row (0-47:64). It has no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no vertical south face and no ellipse. The column scans show only noisy brown and grey ground tones, with dark 1-row outline lines at rows 22, 29, 31 and 43-47 that are texture rather than edges. The three small debris clusters have a few dark rows, but they are scattered details on the flat ground. The whole piece reads as a flat top-down floor decal, which matches the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate soil patch has about 9 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as both references. The earth shows mottled grain and crack lines in several brown steps. The debris (rusty sheet, concrete lumps, shards) is shaded with 4-5 steps and has tinted dark red-brown edges rather than a black sticker outline. Only 3% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is material-toned. Small debris props are scattered over the whole patch, which keeps density even. There are no large flat fills, and the patch reads like the reference ground tiles in craft.

surfaces.part: debris cluster: rusty sheet, concrete lumps, glass shards and cable (upper right)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 64-wide rectangle on every row from 0 to 47. The column scans show only mottled earth and gravel texture, with no front-edge line, eave shadow, or vertical south face anywhere. The darker lines at rows 22, 29, 31 and 43 are cracks in the ground texture, not edges. Three small debris clusters (a sheet with dark outlines, concrete lumps, glass glints and cable) sit on the ground plane as decor. The whole piece is a flat ground decal seen from above with no front face, which is correct for a flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's earth ramp has about 5 steps: mottled mid browns, darker crack lines and stain patches, and lighter grain dots. That is comparable to the grass and paving references. Measured facts support this: 9 visible tones per tile against 3 for grass and 7 for paving, and 0% near-flat coverage, so there are no flat fills. Only 3% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the dark edges lean brown or red-brown, a tinted material tone rather than a black sticker outline. The debris (sheet, concrete lumps, glass, cable) is small, sparse and a little sticker-like with its darker rims. The ground between the debris is varied and textured enough that a careful artist would accept it next to the references without it looking thinner or flatter. Texture is solid but not as clumped or per-stone detailed as the paving, so I rate it 'some' rather than 'rich'.
